blocks.text: Exercises: sentences and translations from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.why: a) The accusative plural of inanimate nouns is the same as the nominative plural: *Вот столы. — Я вижу столы. Вот книги. — Я вижу книги.* b) The accusative plural of animate nouns is the same as the genitive plural: *Это студенты и студентки. — Здесь нет студентов и студенток. — Я знаю студентов и студенток.* — DLI, Lessons 42–45.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: a) The accusative plural of inanimate nouns is the same as the nominative plural: *Вот столы. — Я вижу столы.

exercises.prompt: Tom is a diamond in the rough.
exercises.why: Notes. 1) Three nouns: люди, дети and дочери have the instrumental case ending -ьми instead of -ями: людьми, детьми, дочерьми. 2) Masculine and neuter nouns with the irregular plural ending in -ья (стулья, перья, etc.) retain the «ь»: стульям, стульями, о стульях. — DLI, Lessons 42–45.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.prompt: To stand on your own two feet means to be independent.
exercises.why: For the dative and the prepositional plural there are two kinds of endings for each case: -ам, -ами, -ах after a hard, a sibilant or a guttural consonant; -ям, -ями, -ях after a soft consonant, a «ь» or a vowel. — DLI, Lessons 42–45.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.why: The preposition по is also used in time expressions with the dative plural of nouns in the meaning "on", "in" (repeatedly): *по четвергам* — on Thursdays; *по утрам* — in the mornings. — DLI, Lessons 42–45.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
